### Recruitment and Training

#### Army (enlisted)

[![Image 83](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/Kumaon_Regimental_Centre.jpg/250px-Kumaon_Regimental_Centre.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kumaon_Regimental_Centre.jpg)

Kumaon Regimental Centre, a training centre of GD soldiers for [Kumaon Regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumaon_Regiment "Kumaon Regiment")

The majority of the personnel in the Indian Army are enlisted soldiers, primarily under the Ground Duty (GD) category.[\[107\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-FOOTNOTEIISS2018-110) These personnel are generally deployed to perform combat or combat related roles. The soldiers are inducted into the army under the Agnipath scheme for four years, and 25% of them are retained after four years as permanent cadre. A GD soldier shall have passed class 10 along with matriculation certificate, and must be a citizen of India or Nepal or a subject of Bhutan. The age of the soldier must be 17½ to 21 years, and the candidates shall have no medical ailment or disease and are evaluated for height, weight, vision, hearing, and physical fitness. Fitness tests include a 1.6 km Run, Pull Ups, jumping a 9 Feet ditch, and doing a zig zag balance test.[\[108\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-FOOTNOTEIISS2019-111)

[![Image 84](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/Mechanised_Infantry_Regimental_Centre.jpg/250px-Mechanised_Infantry_Regimental_Centre.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mechanised_Infantry_Regimental_Centre.jpg)

Regimental Centre of Mechanised Infantry, for training of technical and artillery soldiers

The army also recruits personnel for technical roles, such as artillery, signals, aviation technician, nursing assistant, etc. These roles require higher educational qualifications, i.e. Class 12 pass from science stream or diploma qualifications. After selection the candidates are sent for _Basic Military Training_ at regimental centres.[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-112)

#### Military academies

The Indian Armed Forces have set up numerous military academies across India for training personnel. Military Schools, [Sainik Schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sainik_School "Sainik School"), and the [Rashtriya Indian Military College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashtriya_Indian_Military_College "Rashtriya Indian Military College") were founded to broaden the recruitment base of the Defence Forces. The three branches of the Indian Armed Forces jointly operate several institutions such as: the [National Defence Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Defence_Academy_/(India/) "National Defence Academy (India)") (NDA), the [Defence Services Staff College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defence_Services_Staff_College "Defence Services Staff College") (DSSC), the [National Defence College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Defence_College,_India "National Defence College, India") (NDC) and the [College of Defence Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Defence_Management "College of Defence Management") (CDM) for training its officers. The [Armed Forces Medical College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_Medical_College "Armed Forces Medical College") (AFMC) is responsible for providing the entire pool of medical staff to the Armed Forces by giving them in-service training.[\[108\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-FOOTNOTEIISS2019-111)[\[110\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-FOOTNOTEIISS2014-113)

Officer recruitment is through many military-related academies. Besides the tri-service [National Defence Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Defence_Academy_/(India/) "National Defence Academy (India)") (NDA) in [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune "Pune"), the three services have their own training institutes for this purpose. These include: the [Indian Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Military_Academy "Indian Military Academy") (IMA) in [Dehradun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehradun "Dehradun"), the [Indian Naval Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Naval_Academy "Indian Naval Academy") (INA) in [Ezhimala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezhimala "Ezhimala"), the [Air Force Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_Academy,_Dundigul "Air Force Academy, Dundigul") in [Dundigal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dundigal "Dundigal"), the [Officers Training Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officers_Training_Academy "Officers Training Academy") (OTA) in [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai "Chennai") and [Gaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaya,_India "Gaya, India").[\[111\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-yn6j-114)[\[112\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-toi10f-115) Other notable training institutions are the [Army War College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_War_College,_Mhow "Army War College, Mhow") (AWC) in Mhow, Madhya Pradesh, the [High Altitude Warfare School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Altitude_Warfare_School "High Altitude Warfare School") (HAWS) in Gulmarg, Jammu and Kashmir, the [Counter Insurgency and Jungle Warfare School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counter_Insurgency_and_Jungle_Warfare_School "Counter Insurgency and Jungle Warfare School") (CIJW) in Vairengte, Mizoram, and the [College of Military Engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Military_Engineering,_Pune "College of Military Engineering, Pune") (CME) in Pune, Maharashtra. After being commissioned, officers are posted and deputed, and are at the helm of affairs not only inside India but also abroad. Officers are appointed and removed only by the [President of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_India "President of India").[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-116)

### Overseas bases and relations

[![Image 85](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Haa-Dzong_Bhutan.jpg/250px-Haa-Dzong_Bhutan.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Haa-Dzong_Bhutan.jpg)

The Haa Dzong in [Bhutan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhutan "Bhutan") which houses the Headquarters of [Indian Military Training Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Military_Training_Team "Indian Military Training Team") (IMTRAT)

[Farkhor Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farkhor_Air_Base "Farkhor Air Base") is a military air base located near the town of Farkhor in Tajikistan, 130 kilometres (81 mi) southeast of the capital Dushanbe. It is operated by the Indian Air Force in collaboration with the Tajikistan Air Force. Farkhor is India's first and only military base outside its territory.[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-117) There was an unconfirmed report of India building some assets at [Ayni Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayni_Air_Base "Ayni Air Base") in Tajikistan,[\[115\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-118) although the Tajik government has denied this.[\[116\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-119) However, India had deployed its Army and [Border Roads Organisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border_Roads_Organisation "Border Roads Organisation") personnel to upgrade Ayni airbase by extending its runway, constructing an air-traffic control tower and perimeter fencing around the base. India provided medium-lift choppers to Tajikistan and a dedicated hospital there as part of efforts to build on the strategic ties between the two countries against the backdrop of US-led troops pulling out from Afghanistan in 2014.[\[117\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-120) India is also helping with the development of [Chah Bahar Seaport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Chabahar "Port of Chabahar") in southeastern [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran"), which is speculated to be done to secure India's Maritime assets and also as a gateway to Afghanistan & Central Asia. However, India and Israel also have a very strong defence relationship.[\[118\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-121)

[![Image 86](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Indian_Armed_Forces_-_Republic_day_parade_2024.jpg/250px-Indian_Armed_Forces_-_Republic_day_parade_2024.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Indian_Armed_Forces_-_Republic_day_parade_2024.jpg)

All Women Contingent from, all the three services of the Indian Armed Forces

In the [1950 Indo-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_Indo-Nepal_Treaty_of_Peace_and_Friendship "1950 Indo-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship"), India took on the obligation to actively assist Nepal in national defence and military preparedness, and both nations agreed not to tolerate threats to each other's security.[\[119\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-122)[\[120\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-123) In 1958, the then-[Indian Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Prime_Minister "Indian Prime Minister") [Jawaharlal Nehru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jawaharlal_Nehru "Jawaharlal Nehru") visited Bhutan and reiterated India's support for Bhutan's independence and later declared in the [Indian Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Parliament "Indian Parliament") that any aggression against Bhutan would be seen as aggression against India.[\[121\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-BI-124) India started the process to bring the island country Maldives into India's security grid.[\[122\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-125) India is also one of three countries with whom Japan has a security pact, the others being Australia and the United States.[\[123\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-126) India and Russia maintain [strong military co-operation.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo%E2%80%93Russia_relations "Indo–Russia relations") India has defence pacts with the US focusing on areas including security, joint training, joint development and manufacture of defence equipment and technology.[\[124\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-127) In 1951, India and Burma signed a Treaty of Friendship in New Delhi. Article II of the treaty stipulates that "There shall be everlasting peace and unalterable friendship between the two States who shall ever strive to strengthen and develop further the cordial relations existing between the peoples of the two countries."[\[125\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-128) India had signed a pact to develop ports in Myanmar and various bilateral issues, including economic co-operation, connectivity, security and energy.[\[126\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-129) India has a "comprehensive strategic partnership" with UAE.[\[127\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-130) India has maritime security arrangements in place with Oman and Qatar.[\[128\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-131) In 2008, a landmark defence pact was signed, under which India committed its military assets to protect "Qatar from external threats".[\[129\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-132) On 9 June 2012, the JIMEX 2012 naval exercise took place off the coast of Tamil Nadu in India to Tokyo in Japan. This was the first ever bilateral maritime exercise between the two nations in a long time, reflecting their similar interests, especially those involving spontaneous regional security against common external aggressors. The Indian Navy has berthing rights in Oman and Vietnam.

As part of its two-decade-old [Look East policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Look_East_policy_/(India/) "Look East policy (India)"), India has substantially stepped up military engagement with East Asian and [ASEAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASEAN "ASEAN") nations. Although never explicitly stated, ASEAN and East Asian nations want New Delhi to be a counterweight to increasing Chinese footprints in the region. Philippines, Thailand, Indonesia and, particularly, Vietnam and Myanmar have time and again pressed India to help them both in terms of military training and weapons supply.[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-133) Myanmar's Navy Chief, Vice Admiral Thura Thet Swe during his four-day visit to India in late July 2012 held wide-ranging consultations with top officials from the Indian Ministry of Defence. Apart from increasing the number of training slots of Myanmar officers in Indian military training establishments, India has agreed to build at least four Offshore Patrol Vehicles (OPV) in Indian Shipyards to be used by Myanmar's navy. For more than a decade now, India has assisted Vietnam in beefing up its naval and air capabilities. For instance, India has repaired and upgraded more than 100 [MiG 21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikoyan-Gurevich_MiG-21 "Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21") planes of the Vietnam People's Air Force and supplied them with enhanced avionics and radar systems. Indian Air Force pilots have also been training their Vietnamese counterparts. In a first, India has offered a $100-million credit line to Vietnam to purchase military equipment. A bilateral agreement for the use of facilities in India by the Singapore Air Force and Army was signed in October 2007 and August 2008 respectively and has been extended up to 2017. Singapore is the only country to which India is offering such facilities.[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-134)

Indian Army
-----------

Indian Army's [Arjun Mark 1A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjun_/(tank/) "Arjun (tank)") tank.

The Indian Army is a voluntary service, the [military draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_draft "Military draft") having never been imposed in India. It is one of the largest standing armies (and the largest standing volunteer army) in the world, with 1,237,000 active troops and 800,000 reserve troops.[\[132\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-Studies2023-135) The force is headed by the [Chief of Army Staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_Army_Staff_of_the_Indian_Army "Chief of Army Staff of the Indian Army"), General [Upendra Dwivedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_the_Army_Staff_/(India/) "Chief of the Army Staff (India)"). The highest rank in the Indian Army is [Field Marshal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_Marshal "Field Marshal"), but it is a largely ceremonial rank and appointments are made by the [President of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_India "President of India"), on the advice of the [Union Cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Cabinet_of_India "Union Cabinet of India") of Ministers, only in exceptional circumstances. [Sam Manekshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Manekshaw "Sam Manekshaw") and the [K.M. Cariappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_Marshal_Kodandera_Madappa_Cariappa "Field Marshal Kodandera Madappa Cariappa") are the only two officers who have attained this rank.[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-136)[\[134\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-137)

The army has combat experience in diverse terrains and also has a distinguished history of serving in [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") [peacekeeping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacekeeping "Peacekeeping") operations. India contributes 6000 of its personnel to the UN peacekeeping efforts making it the second largest contributor.[\[135\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-138) The Indian Army has seen military action during the [First Kashmir War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Kashmir_War "First Kashmir War"),[\[136\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-139) [Operation Polo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Polo "Operation Polo"),[\[137\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-140) the [Sino-Indian War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sino-Indian_War "Sino-Indian War"),[\[138\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-141) the [Second Kashmir War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Kashmir_War "Second Kashmir War"), the [Indo-Pakistani War of 1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Pakistani_War_of_1971 "Indo-Pakistani War of 1971"), the [Sri Lankan civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lankan_civil_war "Sri Lankan civil war") and the [Kargil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kargil_War "Kargil War"). The Indian Army has participated in several UN [peacekeeping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacekeeping "Peacekeeping") operations including those in: Cyprus, Lebanon, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Angola, Cambodia, Vietnam, Namibia, El Salvador, Liberia, Mozambique and Somalia. The army also provided a [paramedical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramedical "Paramedical") unit to facilitate the withdrawal of the sick and wounded in the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War").

### Doctrine, corps, field force

[![Image 87](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/PIC18Y6S_%28cropped%29.jpg/330px-PIC18Y6S_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PIC18Y6S_/(cropped/).jpg)

Indian Army [Pinaka multi-barrel rocket launcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinaka_multi-barrel_rocket_launcher "Pinaka multi-barrel rocket launcher").

The current combat doctrine of the Indian Army is based on effectively utilising holding formations and strike formations. In the case of an attack, the holding formations would contain the enemy, and strike formations would counter-attack to neutralise enemy forces.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] In the case of an Indian attack, the holding formations would pin enemy forces down while the strike formations attack at a point of India's choosing. The Indian Army is large enough to devote several corps to the strike role. The army is also looking at enhancing its special forces capabilities.[\[139\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-142) With the role of India increasing, and the need to protect India's interests on far-off shores becoming important, the Indian Army and Indian Navy are jointly planning to set up a marine brigade.[\[140\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-143)

The Army's field force comprises fifteen corps, three armoured divisions, four Reorganised Army Plains Infantry Divisions (RAPID), eighteen infantry divisions and ten mountain divisions, a number of independent brigades, and requisite combat support and service support formations and units. Among the fifteen, four are "strike" corps – [Mathura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathura "Mathura") ([I Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Corps_/(India/) "I Corps (India)")), [Ambala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambala_Cantonment "Ambala Cantonment") ([II Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/II_Corps_/(India/) "II Corps (India)")), [Bhopal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhopal "Bhopal") ([XXI Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XXI_Corps_/(India/) "XXI Corps (India)")) and [Panagarh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panagarh "Panagarh") ([XVII Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XVII_Corps_/(India/) "XVII Corps (India)")). The main combat and combat support units are 68 armoured regiments, and over 350 infantry battalions and 300 artillery regiments (including two surface-to-surface missile (SSM) units). Among major armaments and equipment, there are 4,614 main battle tanks, more than 150,000 vehicles, 140 self-propelled artillery, 3,243 towed artillery, more than 700 rocket artillery(MLRS) in the Indian Army.[\[141\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-144)

#### Mountain Strike Corps

India has raised a new mountain strike corps to strengthen its defence along its disputed border with China in the high reaches of the Himalayas. However, the entire XVII Corps, with its headquarters at [Panagarh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panagarh "Panagarh") in [West Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bengal "West Bengal"), will only be fully raised with 90,274 troops at a cost of ₹646.7 billion (equivalent to ₹870 billion or US$10 billion in 2023) by 2018–19. With units spread across the 4,057 kilometres (2,521 mi) Line of Actual Control (LAC) from [Ladakh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladakh "Ladakh") to [Arunachal Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arunachal_Pradesh "Arunachal Pradesh"), the corps will have two high-altitude infantry divisions (59 Div at Panagarh and 72 Div at Pathankot) with their integral units, two independent infantry brigades, two armoured brigades and the like. It will include 30 new infantry battalions and two Para-Special Forces battalions. In other words, it will have "rapid reaction force" capability to launch a counter-offensive into [Tibet Autonomous Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibet_Autonomous_Region "Tibet Autonomous Region") (TAR) in the event of any Chinese attack.[\[142\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-145)

### Army Aviation Corps

[![Image 88](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Rudra_Vayushakti_2024.jpg/250px-Rudra_Vayushakti_2024.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rudra_Vayushakti_2024.jpg)

Indian Army's [HAL Rudra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_Rudra "HAL Rudra") helicopter's.

The [Army Aviation Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_Aviation_Corps_/(India/) "Army Aviation Corps (India)") is another vital part of the Indian Army formed on 1 November 1986. The army aviation pilots are drawn from other combat arms, including artillery officers, to form a composite third dimensional force for an integrated battle. IAF operates and flies attack Helicopters like the Mil Mi-25/Mi-35 which are owned and administered by the Indian Air Force, but under the operational control of the Army and play a major role to support the armoured columns and infantry. Apart from the attack role, helicopters like the [HAL Chetak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_Chetak "HAL Chetak"), [HAL Cheetah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A%C3%A9rospatiale_SA_315B_Lama "Aérospatiale SA 315B Lama"), and [HAL Dhruv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_Dhruv "HAL Dhruv") provide logistical support for the Indian Army in remote and inaccessible areas, especially the Siachen Glacier. To equip Army Aviation Corps, a procurement process for 197 light utility helicopters (LUH) is ongoing,\[_[when?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_\] of which 64 will be used in the Army Aviation Corps to replace the Cheetak and Cheetah Helicopters. [HAL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan_Aeronautics_Limited "Hindustan Aeronautics Limited") has obtained a firm order to deliver 114 HAL [Light Combat Helicopters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_Light_Combat_Helicopter "HAL Light Combat Helicopter") to the Indian Army.[\[143\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-146)

### Modernisation

#### Mechanised forces

[![Image 89](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Yudh_Abhyas-09_T-90.JPG/330px-Yudh_Abhyas-09_T-90.JPG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yudh_Abhyas-09_T-90.JPG)

[Indian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Army "Indian Army")'s tanks and infantry vehicles during an exercise.

India is re-organising its mechanised forces to achieve strategic mobility and high-volume firepower for rapid thrusts into enemy territory. At present, the Indian army has severe deficiencies in its artillery (particularly self-propelled guns) and ammunition stocks, not to mention the inability of some of its modern tanks to operate in the heat and dust of the desert regions around the international border.[\[144\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-Ladwig2-147) India proposes to progressively induct as many as 248 [Arjun MBT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjun_MBT "Arjun MBT") and to develop and induct the Arjun MK-II variant, 1,657 Russian-origin [T-90](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-90 "T-90")S main-battle tanks, apart from the ongoing upgrade of its [T-72](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-72 "T-72") fleet. Arjun MK-II trials had already begun in August 2013.[\[145\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-148) The improved features of the MK-II version of Arjun are night vision capabilities with a thermal imaging system for detecting all kinds of missiles, [Explosive Reactive Armour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Explosive_Reactive_Armour "Explosive Reactive Armour") (ERA), mine ploughs, the ability to fire anti-tank missiles with its 120 mm main gun, an [Advanced Air Defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corps_of_Army_Air_Defence_/(India/) "Corps of Army Air Defence (India)") gun capable of shooting down helicopters with a 360-degree coverage, Automatic Target Tracking (ATT) lending a greater accuracy when it comes to moving targets and superior Laser Warning and Control systems. The Indian Army will upgrade its entire Boyevaya Mashina Pekhoty-2 ([BMP-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMP-2 "BMP-2"))/2K [infantry combat vehicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infantry_combat_vehicle "Infantry combat vehicle") (ICV) fleet to enhance their ability to address operational requirements. Upgrades include integration of the latest generation fire control system, twin missile launchers and commander's thermal imaging panoramic sights, anti- tank guided missiles, as well as automatic grenade launchers.[\[146\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-149)

#### Artillery

Under the Field Artillery Rationalisation Plan, the army plans to procure 3000 to 4000 pieces of artillery at a cost of US$3,000,000,000 (equivalent to $4,049,571,429 in 2024). This includes purchasing 1580 towed, 814 mounted, 180 self-propelled wheeled, 100 self-propelled tracked and 145 ultra-light 155 mm/52 calibre artillery guns. After three years of searching and negotiations, India ordered [M777](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M777_howitzer "M777 howitzer") 155 mm howitzers from USA in September 2013.[\[147\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-150)

To lend greater firepower support to the [Mechanized infantry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanized_infantry "Mechanized infantry"), DRDO has developed the [Pinaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinaka_Multi_Barrel_Rocket_Launcher "Pinaka Multi Barrel Rocket Launcher") [multiple rocket launcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_rocket_launcher "Multiple rocket launcher"). The system has a maximum range of 39–40 kilometres (24–25 mi) and can fire a [salvo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvo "Salvo") of 12 [HE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Explosive_material "Explosive material") rockets in 44 seconds, neutralising a target area of 3.9 square kilometres (1.5 mi2). The system is mounted on a [Tatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatra_cars "Tatra cars") truck for mobility. Pinaka saw service during the [Kargil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kargil_War "Kargil War"),[\[148\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-151) where it was successful in neutralising enemy positions on the mountain tops. It has since been inducted into the Indian Army in large numbers.[\[149\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-st22a13-152)[\[150\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-jj25m13-153)

#### Infantry

[![Image 90](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Indian_Army_personnel_with_a_Mod._Ak_rifle.jpg/250px-Indian_Army_personnel_with_a_Mod._Ak_rifle.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Indian_Army_personnel_with_a_Mod._Ak_rifle.jpg)

Indian Army soldier from [White Knight Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XVI_Corps_/(India/) "XVI Corps (India)"), 2021.

The Indian Army has also embarked on an infantry modernisation programme known as **F**uturistic **In**fantry **S**oldier **A**s a **S**ystem ([F-INSAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-INSAS "F-INSAS")). The infantry soldiers will be equipped with modular weapon systems that will have multiple functions. The core systems include bullet proof helmet and visor. The bullet proof helmet is an integrated assembly equipped with helmet mounted flashlight, thermal sensors and night vision device, miniature computer with audio headsets. The personal clothing of the soldier of the future would be lightweight with a bullet-proof jacket. The futuristic jacket would be waterproof, yet it would be able to breathe. The new attire will enable the troops to carry extra loads and resist the impact of nuclear, chemical and biological warfare. The new uniform will have vests with sensors to monitor the soldier's health parameters and to provide quick medical relief. The weapons sub-system is built around a multi-calibre individual weapon system with the fourth calibre attached to a grenade launcher. These include a 5.56 mm, a 7.62 mm and a new 6.8 mm under development for the first time in India.[\[151\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-154)

In November 2013, the Indian Army moved a step closer to the battlefield of the future, where command networks know the precise location of every soldier and weapon, with whom generals can exchange reports, photos, data and verbal and written communications. Army headquarters called in 14 Indian companies and issued them an expression of interest (EoI) for developing a Battlefield Management System (BMS). The BMS will integrate combat units – armoured, artillery and infantry regiments, infantry battalions, helicopter flights, etc. – into a digital network that will link together all components of the future battlefield. While precise costs are still unclear, vendors competing for the contract say the army expects to pay about Rs 40,000 crore for developing and manufacturing the BMS.[\[152\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-155) However, in 2015, the Indian Army decided to replace the F-INSAS program in favour of two separate projects. The new program will have two components: one arming the modern infantry soldier with the best available assault rifle, carbines and personal equipment such as the helmet and bulletproof vests, the second part is the Battlefield Management Systems (BMS).[\[153\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-156)

Indian Navy
-----------

The Indian Navy is the [naval branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy "Navy") of the Indian armed forces. With more than 142,000 personnel in total, including 7,000 personnel of the [Indian Naval Air Arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Naval_Air_Arm "Indian Naval Air Arm"), 1,200 [Marine Commandos (MARCOS)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MARCOS_/(India/) "MARCOS (India)") and 1,000 personnel of the [Sagar Prahari Bal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagar_Prahari_Bal "Sagar Prahari Bal").[\[154\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-TOI28089355-157)[\[155\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-158) The Indian Navy is one of the world's largest naval forces and developed into a [blue water navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue-water_navy "Blue-water navy").[\[156\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-159)[\[157\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-Ladwig-160) The Indian Navy has a large operational fleet of total 294 vessels consisting of 2 [aircraft carriers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carriers "Aircraft carriers"), 1 [amphibious transport dock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphibious_transport_dock "Amphibious transport dock"), 9 Landing ship tanks, 12 [destroyers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destroyers "Destroyers"), 12 [frigates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frigates "Frigates"), 2 [nuclear-powered attack submarine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_attack_submarine "Nuclear attack submarine"), 17 conventionally powered [attack submarines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_submarines "Attack submarines"), 18 [corvettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corvettes "Corvettes"), 6 [mine countermeasure vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mine_countermeasure_vessel "Mine countermeasure vessel"), 4 [fleet tankers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_tanker "Fleet tanker") and 137 patrol vessels.

### Ships

[![Image 91](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/INS_Vikramaditya_-_02.jpg/330px-INS_Vikramaditya_-_02.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:INS_Vikramaditya_-_02.jpg)

Indian Navy ships in transit led by aircraft carriers [INS _Vikramaditya_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Vikramaditya "INS Vikramaditya") & [INS _Vikrant_ (2013)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Vikrant_/(2013/) "INS Vikrant (2013)")

The Indian navy operates two aircraft carriers- the first is the [INS _Vikramaditya_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Vikramaditya "INS Vikramaditya"), a modified [_Kiev_\-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiev-class_aircraft_carrier "Kiev-class aircraft carrier") ship,[\[158\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-161) and the indigenous [INS _Vikrant_ (2013)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Vikrant_/(2013/) "INS Vikrant (2013)"). The navy also operates one [_Visakhapatnam_\-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visakhapatnam-class_destroyer "Visakhapatnam-class destroyer"), three [_Kolkata_\-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata-class_destroyer "Kolkata-class destroyer"), three [_Delhi_\-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi-class_destroyer "Delhi-class destroyer") and three [_Rajput_\-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajput-class_destroyer "Rajput-class destroyer") guided-missile destroyers. The _Rajput_\-class destroyers will be replaced in the near future by the next-generation [_Visakhapatnam_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visakhapatnam-class_destroyer "Visakhapatnam-class destroyer") (Project 15B destroyers). In addition to destroyers, the navy operates several classes of frigates such as three [_Shivalik_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shivalik-class_frigate "Shivalik-class frigate") (Project 17 class) and six [_Talwar_\-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talwar-class_frigate "Talwar-class frigate") frigates. Seven additional [_Nilgiri_\-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilgiri-class_frigate_/(2019/) "Nilgiri-class frigate (2019)") (Project 17A-class) frigates are on order. The older [_Brahmaputra_\-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahmaputra-class_frigate "Brahmaputra-class frigate") frigates will be replaced systematically one by one as the new classes of frigates are brought into service over the next decade. Smaller littoral zone combatants in service are in the form of corvettes, of which, the Indian Navy operates the [_Kamorta_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamorta-class_corvette "Kamorta-class corvette"), [_Kora_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kora-class_corvette "Kora-class corvette"), [_Khukri_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khukri-class_corvette "Khukri-class corvette"), [_Veer_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veer-class_corvette "Veer-class corvette") and [_Abhay_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhay-class_corvette "Abhay-class corvette") classes. Replenishment tankers such as the _Jyoti_\-class tanker, the [_Aditya_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aditya-class_auxiliary_ship "Aditya-class auxiliary ship") and the new [_Deepak_\-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepak-class_fleet_tanker "Deepak-class fleet tanker") fleet tankers help improve the navy's endurance at sea. These tankers will be the mainstay of the replenishment fleet until the first half of the 21st century.

### Submarines

[![Image 92](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Indian_Navy%27s_TROPEX-2014_%286%29.JPG/330px-Indian_Navy%27s_TROPEX-2014_%286%29.JPG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Indian_Navy%27s_TROPEX-2014_/(6/).JPG)

[INS _Chakra_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_submarine_Nerpa_/(K-152/) "Russian submarine Nerpa (K-152)") is India's nuclear-powered [attack submarine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_submarine "Attack submarine").

The Indian Navy operates a sizeable fleet of [_Sindhughosh_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sindhughosh-class_submarine "Sindhughosh-class submarine") (Russian [Kilo-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilo-class_submarine "Kilo-class submarine") design) and [_Shishumar_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shishumar-class_submarine "Shishumar-class submarine") (German Type 209/1500 design)-class submarines. A nuclear-powered attack submarine [INS _Chakra_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_submarine_Nerpa_/(K-152/) "Russian submarine Nerpa (K-152)") has been leased from Russia. India is completing the construction of six [Scorpène-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorp%C3%A8ne-class_submarine "Scorpène-class submarine") submarines at Mazagon Dockyards Limited (MDL), in Mumbai under technology transfer from French firm DCNS. The new submarines feature [air-independent propulsion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air-independent_propulsion "Air-independent propulsion") and started joining the navy towards the end of 2017; four were in service by the end of 2021. Designed for coastal defence against under-water threats, the 1,750-tonne submarine-submarine-killer (SSK) Scorpène is 67 metres (219 ft 10 in) in length and can dive to a depth of 300 metres (980 ft). According to French naval officials, the submarine can stay at sea for 45 days with a crew of 31.[\[159\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-162) The standard version has six torpedo tubes and anti-shipping missile launchers. Another ambitious project in this regard is the [nuclear-powered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear-powered_submarine "Nuclear-powered submarine") [ballistic missile submarine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballistic_missile_submarine "Ballistic missile submarine") manufacture programme – [_Arihant_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Arihant "INS Arihant") class.

### Weapons systems

[![Image 93](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ab/Brahmos_imds.jpg/330px-Brahmos_imds.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brahmos_imds.jpg)

The Indian Navy's [BrahMos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BrahMos "BrahMos") supersonic anti-ship [cruise missile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cruise_missile "Cruise missile").

In the category of weapon systems, the Indian Navy operates [K Missile family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K_Missile_family "K Missile family") submarine launched ballistic missiles, the [Prithvi-III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithvi-III "Prithvi-III") ballistic ship-launched missile, and a number of land-attack cruise/Anti-ship missiles such as [BrahMos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BrahMos "BrahMos") Supersonic Cruise Missile, [3M-54E/3M-14E Klub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3M-54_Klub "3M-54 Klub") Anti-Ship/Land Attack Cruise Missile (SS-N-27 Sizzler), [Kh-35](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kh-35 "Kh-35") (SS-N-25 SwitchBlade), P-20 (SS-N-2D Styx), [Sea Eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Eagle_/(missile/) "Sea Eagle (missile)") missile and [Gabriel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_/(missile/) "Gabriel (missile)").\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] [Nirbhay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nirbhay "Nirbhay") long-range subsonic cruise missile and [BrahMos Hypersonic Cruise Missile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BrahMos-II "BrahMos-II") are in development. India has also fitted its [P-8I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P-8I "P-8I") Neptune reconnaissance aircraft with all-weather, [active-rader-homing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Active_radar_homing "Active radar homing"), over-the-horizon [AGM-84L Harpoon Block II Missiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harpoon_/(missile/) "Harpoon (missile)") and Mk 54 All-Up-Round Lightweight Torpedoes.[\[160\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-163) Indian warships' primary air-defence shield is provided by [Barak-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barak_1_/(missile/) "Barak 1 (missile)") SAM, while an advanced version [Barak-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barak-8 "Barak-8"), developed in collaboration with Israel, has entered service.[\[161\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-164) India's next-generation Scorpène-class submarines will be armed with the [Exocet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exocet "Exocet") anti-ship missile system. Among indigenous missiles, a ship-launched version of [Prithvi-II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithvi_/(missile/) "Prithvi (missile)") is called the [Dhanush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhanush_/(missile/) "Dhanush (missile)"), which has a range of 350 kilometres (220 mi) and can carry a nuclear warhead.[\[162\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-165)

### Naval Air Arm

[![Image 94](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/Boeing_P-8I_of_the_Indian_Navy.jpg/330px-Boeing_P-8I_of_the_Indian_Navy.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Boeing_P-8I_of_the_Indian_Navy.jpg)

An Indian Navy [P-8I Neptune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_P-8_Poseidon "Boeing P-8 Poseidon") anti-submarine warfare aircraft.

The [Indian Naval Air Arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Naval_Air_Arm "Indian Naval Air Arm") is a branch of Indian Navy which is tasked to provide an aircraft carrier based strike capability, fleet air defence, maritime reconnaissance, and anti-submarine warfare. Flag Officer Naval Aviation (FONA) at Goa directs the field operations of the air arm. Naval Air Arm operates eight [Tu-142](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tu-142 "Tu-142") aircraft, which entered service in 1988. Upgrading of the aircraft is taking place, which helps to extend the service life of the aircraft by sixteen years. The [BAE Sea Harrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAE_Sea_Harrier "BAE Sea Harrier") operates from the INS Viraat. The BAE Sea Harrier FRS Mk.51 / T Mk.60 fly with the [INAS 300](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INAS_300 "INAS 300") and [INAS 552](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INAS_552 "INAS 552") squadrons of the Indian Navy. The [Mikoyan MiG-29K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikoyan_MiG-29K "Mikoyan MiG-29K") will be deployed aboard INS _Vikramaditya_. The Indian Navy operates five [Il-38](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il-38 "Il-38") planes. They are being upgraded to use Sea Dragon suite. Used principally for anti-submarine warfare (ASW) and search and rescue roles, the helicopter fleet of [Westland Sea King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westland_Sea_King "Westland Sea King") and the Sikorsky [SH-3 Sea King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SH-3_Sea_King "SH-3 Sea King") operate from [INS Garuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Garuda "INS Garuda") (Kochi) as well as INS Kunjali-II (Mumbai) air stations.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] 56 more naval utility helicopters are planned to be inducted from 2016. These will be used for surveillance, anti-submarine warfare, electronic intelligence gathering and search and rescue operations. The helicopters will be equipped with 70 mm rocket launchers, 12.7 mm guns, lightweight torpedoes and depth charges.[\[163\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-166) The Indian Navy will also continue to procure [HAL Dhruv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_Dhruv "HAL Dhruv") as a multi-role utility platform. In the long-range maritime reconnaissance (LRMR) role, the navy uses Boeing [P-8I Neptune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P-8_Poseidon "P-8 Poseidon") and has issued a global tender for nine medium-range maritime reconnaissance (MRMR) aircraft for coastal defence.[\[164\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-167)

### Defence satellite

India's first exclusive defence satellite [GSAT-7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GSAT-7 "GSAT-7") was successfully launched by European space consortium Arianespace's Ariane 5 rocket from Kourou spaceport in [French Guiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Guiana "French Guiana") in August 2013, giving a major push to the country's maritime security. The Indian Navy is the user of the multi-band, home-built communication spacecraft, which is operational. GSAT-7 was designed and developed by the [Indian Space Research Organisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Space_Research_Organisation "Indian Space Research Organisation") (ISRO) and is expected to operate for seven years in its orbital slot at 74 degrees east, providing [UHF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UHF "UHF"), [S-band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S-band "S-band"), [C-band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_band_/(IEEE/) "C band (IEEE)") and [Ku-band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ku-band "Ku-band") relay capacity. Its Ku-band capacity is expected to provide high-density data transmission facility both for voice and video. This satellite has been provided with additional power to communicate with smaller and mobile (not necessarily land-based) terminals. This dedicated satellite is expected to provide the Indian navy with an approximately 3,500–4,000 kilometres (2,200–2,500 mi) footprint over the Indian Ocean region, and over both the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal region and enable real-time networking of all its operational assets in the water (and land). It also will help the navy to operate in a network-centric atmosphere.[\[165\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-168)

Ships from the Indian navy, Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force, and United States Navy during [exercise Malabar 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malabar_/(naval_exercise/) "Malabar (naval exercise)").

India often conducts naval exercises with other friendly countries designed to increase naval interoperability and also to strengthen cooperative security relationships. Some exercises take place annually like: the _Varuna_ with the French Navy, _Konkan_ with the Royal Navy, _Indra_ with Russian Navy, _[Malabar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exercise_Malabar "Exercise Malabar")_ with the US and Japan navies, _Simbex_ with the Republic of Singapore Navy and _[IBSAMAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBSAMAR "IBSAMAR")_ with the Brasil and South African navies. India has also held naval exercise with Vietnam, the Philippines and New Zealand. In 2007, India and South Korea decided to conduct annual naval exercises and India participated in the South Korean international fleet review. In addition, the Indian Navy will also be increasing naval co-operation with other allies, particularly with Germany, and Arab states of the Persian Gulf including Kuwait, Oman,[\[166\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-169) Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.[\[167\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-170) Indian Navy also took part in the world's largest naval exercise/war-game [RIMPAC 2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exercise_RIMPAC "Exercise RIMPAC") along with 22 other nations[\[168\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-171) and has since taken part in RIMPAC each year.

### Modernisation

[![Image 96](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/IAC-1_Vikrant_going_for_its_maiden_sea_trials.jpg/330px-IAC-1_Vikrant_going_for_its_maiden_sea_trials.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:IAC-1_Vikrant_going_for_its_maiden_sea_trials.jpg)

[INS _Vikrant_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Vikrant_/(2013/) "INS Vikrant (2013)") is the Indian Navy's first indigenous aircraft carrier, shown here during its maiden sea trials, August 2021.

In recent years, the Indian Navy has undergone [modernisation and expansion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Navy#Ongoing_expansion "Indian Navy") with the intention of countering growing Chinese maritime power in the Indian Ocean and reaching the status of a recognised [blue-water navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue-water_navy "Blue-water navy").[\[169\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-172)[\[170\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-173) New equipment programmes include: the lease of a nuclear-powered submarine INS _Chakra_ from Russia, the ex-Soviet carrier [INS _Vikramaditya_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Vikramaditya "INS Vikramaditya") and the first of the indigenously built [_Arihant_\-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Arihant "INS Arihant") ballistic missile submarines by 2016, the first of the Scorpène-class submarines by 2016 and the indigenously built aircraft carrier [INS _Vikrant_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikrant-class_aircraft_carrier "Vikrant-class aircraft carrier") by 2018. The plan in the near future is to have two aircraft carriers at sea at all times, with a third docked up in maintenance.[\[171\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-174) Other programmes include the _Talwar_ and _Shivalik_ frigates and the _Kolkata_\-class destroyers, all of which will be equipped with the [BrahMos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BrahMos "BrahMos") cruise missile. In a significant step towards India's pursuit for self-reliance in indigenous warship building, four anti-submarine _Kamorta_\-class stealth corvettes with features such as an [X Form Hull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_/(watercraft/)#Hull_shapes "Hull (watercraft)") and inclined sides for low [radar cross-section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radar_cross-section "Radar cross-section"), [infra-red suppression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrared_signature "Infrared signature"), and [acoustic quieting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoustic_quieting "Acoustic quieting") systems are being built for the Indian Navy.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

[![Image 97](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/Visakhapatnam_%28D66%29_-_P15B_destroyer_of_Indian_Navy_during_sea_trials.jpg/250px-Visakhapatnam_%28D66%29_-_P15B_destroyer_of_Indian_Navy_during_sea_trials.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Visakhapatnam_/(D66/)_-_P15B_destroyer_of_Indian_Navy_during_sea_trials.jpg)

[Guided missile destroyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guided_missile_destroyer "Guided missile destroyer") [D66](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Visakhapatnam "INS Visakhapatnam").

Recent induction of the attack submarine INS _Chakra_, and the development of INS _Arihant_, make the Indian Navy one of six navies worldwide capable of building and operating nuclear-powered submarines.[\[172\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-175) (Others include: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States.) India also launched a 37,500-ton indigenous aircraft carrier [INS _Vikrant_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Vikrant_/(2013/) "INS Vikrant (2013)") in August 2013 in its bid to join a select group of nations – the United States, the United Kingdom, Russia and France – capable of building such warships. It will undergo extensive tests in the next few years before it is commissioned into the navy. INS _Vikrant_, is expected to carry [MiG 29K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MiG-29K "MiG-29K") fighters and light combat aircraft such as the [HAL Tejas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_Tejas "HAL Tejas").

India is also set to become the first country to buy a military aircraft from Japan since World War II. India is expected to sign a deal for the purchase of six Utility [Seaplane Mark 2 (US-2)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ShinMaywa_US-2 "ShinMaywa US-2") amphibian aircraft when Prime Minister [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi") visits Japan from 31 August – 3 September 2014. The 47-tonne US-2 aircraft does not require a long airstrip to take off or to land. It is capable of taking off from land and water (300 metres (330 yd)-stretch). It can carry loads of up to 18 tonnes and can be engaged in search and rescue operations. With a range of over 4,500 kilometres (2,800 mi) it can patrol areas 1,800 kilometres (1,100 mi) away and react to an emergency by landing 30 armed troops even in waves as high as 10 feet (3.0 m).[\[173\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-176)

Indian Air Force
----------------

The Indian Air Force is the air arm of the Indian armed forces. Its primary responsibility is to secure Indian [airspace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airspace "Airspace") and to conduct [aerial warfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerial_warfare "Aerial warfare") during a conflict. It was officially established on 8 October 1932 as an auxiliary air force of the [British Raj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") and the prefix _Royal_ was added in 1945 in recognition of its services during World War II. After India achieved independence from the United Kingdom in 1947, the [Royal Indian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Indian_Air_Force "Royal Indian Air Force") served the [Dominion of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominion_of_India "Dominion of India"), with the prefix being dropped when India became a republic in 1950. The Indian Air Force plays a crucial role in securing Indian airspace and also in India's power projection in South Asia and Indian Ocean. Therefore, modernising and expanding the Indian Air Force is a top priority for the Indian government. Over the years, the IAF has grown from a tactical force to one with transoceanic reach. The strategic reach emerges from induction of Force Multipliers like Flight Refuelling Aircraft (FRA), Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) and credible strategic lift capabilities.

### Aircraft

[![Image 98](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Su-30_MKI_firing_Brahmos-ER.jpg/250px-Su-30_MKI_firing_Brahmos-ER.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Su-30_MKI_firing_Brahmos-ER.jpg)

IAF [Sukhoi Su-30MKI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukhoi_Su-30MKI "Sukhoi Su-30MKI") firing [BrahMos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BrahMos "BrahMos")\-ER

Historically, the IAF has generally relied on Soviet, British, Israeli and French military craft and technology to support its growth. IAF's primary air superiority fighter with the additional capability to conduct air-ground (strike) missions is [Sukhoi Su-30MKI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukhoi_Su-30MKI "Sukhoi Su-30MKI"). The IAF have placed an order for a total of 272 Su-30MKIs of which 205 are in service as of May 2015.[\[174\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-FOOTNOTESubramaniam2017-177) The Mikoyan [MiG-29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MiG-29 "MiG-29") is a dedicated air superiority fighter, and constitutes a second line of defence after the Sukhoi Su-30MKI. At present, 66 MiG-29s are in service, all of which are being upgraded to the MiG-29UPG standard. The [Dassault Mirage 2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dassault_Mirage_2000 "Dassault Mirage 2000") is the primary multirole fighter in service and the IAF operates 49 Mirage 2000Hs which are being upgraded to the Mirage 2000-5 MK2 standard. As part of the upgrade, the aircraft will also be equipped with MBDA's [MICA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MICA_/(missile/) "MICA (missile)") family of medium-range missiles.[\[175\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-178) To give the IAF fighters an edge in anti-ship and land attack roles, a smaller version of [BrahMos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BrahMos "BrahMos") missile is being developed to be integrated in Sukhoi Su-30MKI[\[176\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-179) and is expected to be delivered to IAF by 2015.[\[177\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-180)

[![Image 99](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Indian_Air_Force_Rafale.jpg/250px-Indian_Air_Force_Rafale.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Indian_Air_Force_Rafale.jpg)

IAF [Rafale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dassault_Rafale "Dassault Rafale") at [Bordeaux–Mérignac Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux%E2%80%93M%C3%A9rignac_Airport "Bordeaux–Mérignac Airport"), 6 February 2020

In the aerial refuelling (tanker) role, the IAF operates six [Ilyushin Il-78](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilyushin_Il-78 "Ilyushin Il-78")MKIs. For strategic military transport operations the IAF uses the [Ilyushin Il-76](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilyushin_Il-76 "Ilyushin Il-76"), and has placed orders for 10 Boeing [C-17 Globemaster III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-17_Globemaster_III "C-17 Globemaster III"), four of which were [delivered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-17_Globemaster_III#Indian_Air_Force "C-17 Globemaster III") by November 2013. The [C-130J Super-Hercules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Martin_C-130J_Super_Hercules "Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules") planes of the IAF is used by special forces for combined Army-Air Force operations. There are six C-130Js in service and six more are planned to be procured.[\[178\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-181) The [Antonov An-32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonov_An-32 "Antonov An-32") serves as medium transport aircraft in the IAF.

As an airborne early warning system, the IAF operates the Israeli EL/W-2090 [Phalcon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EL/M-2075 "EL/M-2075") Airborne Early Warning and Control System [AEW&C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AEW%26C "AEW&C"). A total of three such systems are in service, with possible orders for two more.[\[179\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-182) The [DRDO AEW&CS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DRDO_AEW%26CS "DRDO AEW&CS") is a project of India's DRDO to develop an AEW&C system for the Indian Air Force. The DRDO AEWACS programme aims to deliver three radar-equipped surveillance aircraft to the Indian Air Force. The aircraft platform selected was the [Embraer ERJ 145](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embraer_ERJ_145_family "Embraer ERJ 145 family"). Three ERJ 145 were procured from Embraer at a cost of US$300 Million, including the contracted modifications to the airframe. Probable delivery date for the first batch of three is 2015.[\[180\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-183)

### Network-centric warfare

[![Image 100](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/DrdoNetra.jpg/330px-DrdoNetra.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DrdoNetra.jpg)

[DRDO AEW&CS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DRDO_AEW%26CS "DRDO AEW&CS").

The Indian Air Force (IAF) made progress towards becoming a truly network-centric air force with the integration of [Air Force Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_Network "Air Force Network") (AFNET), a reliable and robust digital information grid that enables accurate and faster response to enemy threats, in 2010.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] The modern, state-of-the-art AFNET is a fully secure communication network, providing IAF a critical link among its command and control centre, sensors such as the Airborne Early Warning and Control Systems, and attack platforms such as fighter aircraft and missile launchers. Integrated Air Command and Control System (IACCS), an automated command and control system for Air Defence (AD) operations will ride the AFNet backbone integrating all ground-based and airborne sensors, AD weapon systems and C2 nodes.

[![Image 101](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/C-130_J.jpg/330px-C-130_J.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:C-130_J.jpg)

A [C-130 J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Martin_C-130J_Super_Hercules "Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules") tactical transport aircraft.

Subsequent integration with other services networks and civil radars will provide an integrated Air Situation Picture to operators to carry out Air Defence role. AFNet will prove to be an effective [force multiplier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force_multiplier "Force multiplier") for intelligence analysis, mission planning and control, post-mission feedback and related activities like maintenance, logistics and administration. A comprehensive design with multi-layer security precautions for "Defence in Depth" have been planned by incorporating encryption technologies, Intrusion Prevention Systems to ensure the resistance of the IT system against information manipulation and eavesdropping.[\[181\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-184)

In October 2013, IAF launched its own stand-alone ₹3 Billion (US$34 Million) cellular network, through which secure video calling and other information exchange facilities will be provided. The IAF also plans to issue around one hundred thousand mobile handsets to its personnel of the rank of sergeant and above to connect and provide secure 'end-point' connectivity to airborne forces deployed across the country. The captive network has been named 'Air Force Cellular'. While Phase I of the project will ensure mobile connectivity to all air combat units in the [National Capital Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Capital_Region_/(India/) "National Capital Region (India)"), its Phase II will cover the rest of the bases.[\[182\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-185)

### Modernisation

The [Medium Multi-Role Combat Aircraft (MMRCA) competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_MRCA_competition "Indian MRCA competition"), also known as the MRCA tender, was a competition to supply 126 multi-role combat aircraft to the Indian Air Force (IAF). The Defence Ministry has allocated ~ US$13 billion for the purchase of these aircraft, making it India's single largest defence deal.[\[183\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-186) On 31 January 2012, it was announced that [Dassault Rafale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dassault_Rafale "Dassault Rafale") won the competition due to its lower life-cycle cost. However the tender was cancelled in July 2015.[\[184\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-187) The Indian Air Force (IAF) is also in the final stages of acquiring 22 [Apache Longbow gunships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AH-64_Apache "AH-64 Apache"), armed with [Hellfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellfire_missile "Hellfire missile") and Stinger missiles in a $1.2 billion contract and 15 heavy-lift [Boeing CH Chinook helicopters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinook_helicopter "Chinook helicopter").[\[185\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-economictimes.indiatimes.com-188) The IAF has initiated the process for acquisition of additional [Mi-17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi-17 "Mi-17") IV helicopters, heavy lift helicopters, Advanced Light Helicopter and Light Combat Helicopters. Among trainer aircraft, the [Hawk Advanced Jet Trainer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAE_Systems_Hawk "BAE Systems Hawk") has been inducted and the [Intermediate Jet Trainer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_HJT-36_Sitara "HAL HJT-36 Sitara") (IJT) would be acquired in the near future.

[HAL Tejas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_Tejas "HAL Tejas") firing [Astra (missile)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astra_/(missile/) "Astra (missile)")

In recent times, India has also manufactured its own aircraft such as the HAL Tejas, a 4th generation fighter, and the HAL Dhruv, a [multi-role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utility_helicopter "Utility helicopter") helicopter, which has been exported to several countries, including Israel, Burma, Nepal and Ecuador. A weaponised version of Dhruv is called the HAL Rudra, which is armed with high-velocity M621 20 mm cannon, long-range 70 mm rockets (8 km), air-to-air missiles (Mistral-II), and MAWS (missile approach warning system).[\[186\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-189) [Combat in Kargil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kargil_War "Kargil War") highlighted the requirement of an attack helicopter specially made for such high-altitude operations. The [HAL Light Combat Helicopter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_Light_Combat_Helicopter "HAL Light Combat Helicopter") (LCH) is a multi-role combat helicopter being developed in India by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) for use by the Indian Air Force and the Indian Army. The LCH is being designed to fit into an anti-infantry and anti-armour role and will be able to operate at high altitudes.[\[187\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-190) LCH will be fitted with indigenous anti-tank missile [Helina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nag_/(missile/) "Nag (missile)").

India also maintains [unmanned aerial vehicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_aerial_vehicle "Unmanned aerial vehicle") (UAV) squadrons (primarily [Searcher-II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAI_Searcher "IAI Searcher") and [Heron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAI_Heron "IAI Heron") from Israel) which can be used to carry out ground and aerial surveillance.[\[188\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-191) India is also testing its own long-range [Beyond Visual Range missile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyond_Visual_Range_missile "Beyond Visual Range missile")| (BVR) an air-to-air missile named [Astra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astra_Missile "Astra Missile"),[\[189\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-192) and also building a Medium Altitude Long Endurance Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) called [Rustom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DRDO_Rustom "DRDO Rustom").[\[190\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-193)

India is also in an ambitious collaboration programme with Russia to build [fifth-generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth-generation_jet_fighter "Fifth-generation jet fighter") fighter aircraft, called [HAL/Sukhoi FGFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FGFA "FGFA") which will be based on the Russian [Sukhoi Su-57](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukhoi_Su-57 "Sukhoi Su-57") fighter. Earlier in 2013, the two sides completed the preliminary design of the FGFA and are now negotiating a detailed design contract.[\[191\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-194) Although there is no reliable information about the Su-57 and FGFA specifications yet, it is known from interviews with individuals in the Russian Air Force that it will be [stealthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stealth_aircraft "Stealth aircraft"), have the ability to [supercruise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercruise "Supercruise"), be outfitted with the next generation of air-to-air, air-to-surface, and air-to-ship missiles, and incorporate an [AESA radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AESA_radar "AESA radar").

Joint co-development and co-production of [Multi-role Transport Aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UAC/HAL_Il-214 "UAC/HAL Il-214") (MTA), by Russian partners and HAL, is being launched to meet the requirements of the Russian and Indian Air Forces. The aircraft will be designed for the roles of a 15–20 ton cargo / troop transport, paratrooping / airdrop of supplies including Low Altitude Parachute Extraction System (LAPES) capability. It will be configured such that all types of cargo can be transported, and the aircraft would be capable of operating from semi-prepared runways. The MTA is expected to replace the Indian Air Force's ageing fleet of [Antonov An-32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonov_An-32 "Antonov An-32") transport aircraft. The aircraft is expected to conduct its first flight by 2017, and to enter service by 2018.[\[192\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-195)\[_[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_\]

To protect IAF assets on the ground, there has been a search for short-range surface-to-air missile. India has begun deploying six [Akash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akash_/(missile/) "Akash (missile)") surface-to-air missile (SAM) squadrons in the northeast to deter Chinese jets, helicopters and drones against any misadventure in the region. The IAF has started taking delivery of the six Akash missile squadrons, which can "neutralise" multiple targets at a 25 kilometres (16 mi) interception range in all weather conditions, earmarked for the eastern theatre. The IAF has already deployed the first two Akash squadrons at the Mirage-2000 base in Gwalior and the Sukhoi base in Pune.[\[193\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-196)

Indian Coast Guard
------------------

[![Image 102](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Indian_Coast_Guard_Chetak_Helicopter_picking_up_survivors_from_water_during_a_mock_drill_during_SAREX_2014_%282%29.jpg/330px-Indian_Coast_Guard_Chetak_Helicopter_picking_up_survivors_from_water_during_a_mock_drill_during_SAREX_2014_%282%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Indian_Coast_Guard_Chetak_Helicopter_picking_up_survivors_from_water_during_a_mock_drill_during_SAREX_2014_/(2/).jpg)

[Indian Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Coast_Guard "Indian Coast Guard") (ICG) helicopter takes a survivor to an ICG ship during a mock drill.

The Indian Coast Guard (ICG) protects India's maritime interests and enforces maritime law, with jurisdiction over the territorial waters of India, including its contiguous zone and [exclusive economic zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclusive_economic_zone "Exclusive economic zone"). The Indian Coast Guard was formally established on 18 August 1978 by the Coast Guard Act, 1978 of the Parliament of India as an independent Armed force of India. It operates under the Ministry of Defence.[\[194\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-197)

The Coast Guard works in close co-operation with the Indian Navy, the Department of Fisheries, the Department of Revenue (Customs) and the Central and State police forces.

Central Armed Police Forces
---------------------------

[![Image 103](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/A_Indian_CRPF_QRT_operator.jpg/250px-A_Indian_CRPF_QRT_operator.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A_Indian_CRPF_QRT_operator.jpg)

[![Image 104](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/A_Senior_CoBRA_Force_Officer.jpg/250px-A_Senior_CoBRA_Force_Officer.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A_Senior_CoBRA_Force_Officer.jpg)

A [CRPF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Reserve_Police_Force "Central Reserve Police Force") commando with the [IWI Tavor X95](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IWI_Tavor_X95 "IWI Tavor X95").

The following are the seven paramilitary police forces termed as [Central Armed Police Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Armed_Police_Forces "Central Armed Police Forces") (CAPFs).[\[195\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-198)[\[196\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-199) These forces were earlier referred to as the "central paramilitary forces". In 2011, the nomenclature CAPF was adopted to refer them.[\[197\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-200)[\[198\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-201)

### Assam Rifles

The Assam Rifles trace their lineage to a [paramilitary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramilitary "Paramilitary") police force that was formed under the British in 1835 called _Cachar Levy_. Since then the Assam Rifles have undergone a number of name changes before the name Assam Rifles was finally adopted in 1917.[\[199\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-202) Over the course of its history, the Assam Rifles, and its predecessor units, have served in a number of roles, conflicts and theatres including World War I where they served in Europe and the Middle East, and World War II where they served mainly in Burma. In the post-World War II period, the Assam Rifles have expanded greatly as has their role. There are currently 46 battalions[\[200\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-History-203) of Assam Rifles under the control of the Indian [Ministry of Home Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Home_Affairs_/(India/) "Ministry of Home Affairs (India)") (MHA). They perform many roles including: the provision of internal security under the control of the army through the conduct of counter insurgency and border security operations, provision of aid to the civil power in times of emergency, and the provision of communications, medical assistance and education in remote areas.[\[201\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-Sharma-204) In times of war they can also be used as a combat force to secure rear areas if needed.

### Central Reserve Police Force

Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) is the largest of the CAPFs with 325,000 personnel in 246 [battalions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battalion "Battalion").[\[202\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-205)[\[203\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-206)[\[204\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-207) The CRPF includes the [Rapid Action Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_Action_Force "Rapid Action Force") (RAF), a 15 battalion anti-riot force trained to respond to sectarian violence, and the [Commando Battalion for Resolute Action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commando_Battalion_for_Resolute_Action "Commando Battalion for Resolute Action") (COBRA), a 10 battalion strong anti-[Naxalite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naxalite "Naxalite") force.[\[205\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-208)[\[206\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-209)

### Border Security Force

[![Image 105](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Women_personnel_of_India%27s_Border_Security_Force.jpg/250px-Women_personnel_of_India%27s_Border_Security_Force.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Women_personnel_of_India%27s_Border_Security_Force.jpg)

Women personnel of [Border Security Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border_Security_Force "Border Security Force") at [Attari-Wagah border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wagah-Attari_border_ceremony "Wagah-Attari border ceremony").

The primary role of the Border Security Force (BSF) is to guard the land borders of the country, except the mountains. The sanctioned strength is 265,277 personnel in 193 battalions,[\[207\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-210)[\[208\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-211)[\[209\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-212)[\[210\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-auto1-213) and is headed by an [Indian Police Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Police_Service "Indian Police Service") officer.

### Indo-Tibetan Border Police

The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) is deployed for guard duties on the border with China from Karakoram Pass in Ladakh to Diphu La in Arunachal Pradesh covering a total distance of 2,488 kilometres (1,546 mi).[\[211\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-214) It has 90,000 personnel in 60 battalions.[\[212\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-hindustantimes1-215)[\[213\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-216)[\[214\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-217)

### Sashastra Seema Bal

The objective of the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) is to guard the Indo-Nepal and Indo-Bhutan Borders. As of 2019, it has 94,261 active personnel in 73 battalions and a strength of 98,965 is sanctioned.[\[215\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-218)

### Central Industrial Security Force

One of the largest industrial security forces in the world, the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) provides security to various [public sector companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_sector_undertakings_in_India "Public sector undertakings in India") (PSUs) and other critical infrastructure installations across the country, such as airports. It has a total strength of about 144,418 personnel in 132 battalions.[\[216\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-219)[\[217\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-220)[\[210\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-auto1-213)

### National Security Guard

The [National Security Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Guard "National Security Guard") (NSG) is an elite counter-terrorist and rapid response force. Its roles include conducting anti-sabotage checks, rescuing hostages, neutralising terrorist threats to vital installations, engaging terrorists, responding to hijacking and piracy and protecting VIPs. It has 8636 personnel (including 1086 personnel for regional hubs.[\[218\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces#cite_note-221)). The NSG also includes the _Special Ranger Group_ (SRG), whose 3,000 personnel provide protection to India's VVIPs.\[_[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_\]
