As per the ASSOCHAM-Mahindra SSG study, the reporting of cyber crimes in Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka went up by 117 per cent during 2012-13 causing havoc in the financial space, security establishment and social fabric, dnaindia.com reports on February 9. According to the joint study on “Cyber and Network Security Framework”, in 2013, 681 cyber crime related cases were registered in Maharashtra, which saw a 44.6 per cent rise in cyber crimes when compared to 2012. Andhra Pradesh with 635 cases registered in 2013 also saw a 48 per cent rise when compared to 2012. Karnataka with 513 cases registered in 2013 saw a 24.5 per cent rise compared to 2012. Uttar Pradesh with 372 cases registered in 2013 is in the fourth place. Kerala is in the 5th place with 349 cases registered in 2013, highlights the study. Tamil Nadu and Bihar have very few cyber crime related cases with just 54 cases registered in Tamil Nadu and 23 cases in Bihar in 2013. Gujarat and Odisha have also registered just 61 and 63 cases respectively in 2013. Among the Union Territories, the national capital Delhi has registered 131 cyber crime related cases. It has seen a rise of 72.4 per cent when compared to 2012. D.S Rawat, Secretary General ASSOCHAM said, “What is causing more concern is that the origin of these crimes is widely based abroad in countries including China, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Algeria among others”. “Phishing attacks of online banking accounts or cloning of ATM/Debit cards are common occurrences. The increasing use of mobile/smart-phones/tablets for online banking/financial transactions has also increased the vulnerabilities to a great extent. The maximum offenders came from the 18-30 age group”, adds the report. **Read less...**

Such a counselling facility, if found feasible in the Indian context, will enable parents, teachers and friends of "vulnerable and indoctrinated" youth to seek professional help for their "deradicalisation". Keen to have a domestic counter-radicalisation/deradicalisation policy in place to stem the growing appeal of terror outfits among young Muslims, the Indian security establishment has started examining the best practices followed around the world to wean off sections attracted to jihadi ideology. This includes the US' counter-radicalisation program focused on community outreach, UK's Prevent and Channel programmes as well as Austria's latest deradicalisation counselling initiative. A senior officer of the Indian government said that while US and UK's deradicalization programmes appear to have met with limited success, the Austrian helpline centre, which is not linked to the police but manned by non-profit groups, has got an encouraging response within a couple of months of its launch. The deradicalization centre also conducts educational lectures and puts out material to help identify potential threats. According to a Senior UHM official, a study of impact of deradicalization policies of the US and UK indicates an element of mistrust among their respective Muslim communities, with many members seeing these as a masked effort at "spying". There have been many cases of recidivism among the deradicalised terror recruits. While the US' counter-radicalization efforts are focused on working with the communities to report suspicious activity, the UK's Prevent program seeks to prevent people from being drawn into terrorism through proper advice and support. 'Prevent' works with sectors like education, criminal justice, faith, charities and online where there are risks of radicalization to be dealt with. A linked initiative called Channel helps to fight radicalization by giving individuals access to health and education, specialist mentoring and diversionary activities. **Read less...**

India and the US on February 12 pledged to jointly target financial networks and fund raising by Pakistan-based terrorist organisations as also the D-Company of fugitive underworld don Dawood Ibrahim, reports Deccan Chronicle. The two nations vowed to work together to check illicit money transfers for terrorism, money laundering and other illegal activities. The agreement came at a meeting of the 5th Indo-US Economic and Financial Partnership dialogue, which was attended by the US Treasury Secretary Jacob J Lew and Indian Finance Minister Arun Jaitley. Besides Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and November 26, 2008 (26/11) Mumbai terror attack mastermind Hafiz Saeed's Jam'mat-ud-Dawa (JuD), the two nations identified Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM), the Haqqani Network, D-Company, al Qaida and Islamic State (IS) among terror networks whose funding have to be cut off. "We reiterated our commitment to target the financial networks and fund raising activities of terrorist organisations such as LeT, JuD, Jaishe-e-Mohammad, the Haqqani Network, D-Company, Al Qaida, ISIL, and individual terrorists associated with these organisations," said the statement. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Raghuram Rajan and US Federal Reserve Vice Chairman Stanley Fischer too attended the deliberations that agreed for information sharing between two countries and cooperation on anti-money laundering and terror financing. At a joint press interaction, Lew said the two nations "share a common commitment to working together to try as much as we can to shut down the flow of funding to those who commit terrorist act and other kinds of activities". "We discussed money laundering and funding of terrorism, since a large number of these funds come through concealed identities. This issue has been brought to out notice and the concerned authorities, including central bank, has taken appropriate action in this matter," Jaitley said. "We welcomed the agreements made for information sharing between the two countries' regulatory agencies. We welcomed the prospect of an increasingly robust dialogue and meaningful cooperation on anti-money laundering and combating the financing of terrorism with the signing of the India-US Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in January 2015. **Read less...**

The PIL says the Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India at Hoshangabad practically printed fake notes. An internal inquiry conducted by a former Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) director had also indicted top officials at the government-run mint for the lapse. [Defence ministry signs Rs 1,752 cr deal for remote control guns](https://excelindiaonline.in/defence-ministry/)
================================================================================================================

 [![Image 2](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/b6b59ea67da723f5e6d09ffbfa3d38fd?s=96&d=mm&r=g) Rama Krishna Sangem](https://excelindiaonline.in/author/admin/) 2 years ago

![Image 3: Remote guns](https://excelindiaonline.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Remote-guns-Aweil.jpg)

**Rama Krishna Sangem**

**The Ministry of Defence (MoD)**  has signed a contract on February 14, 2024 with **Advanced Weapon Equipment India Ltd.** **(AWEIL**), Kanpur for manufacturing & supply of a total of 463 indigenously manufactured 12.7 mm Stabilised Remote Control Guns (SRCG) for the Indian Navy & Indian Coast Guard at a total cost of **Rs. 1752.13 crore,** with Indigenous Content (IC) of more than 85%.

The SRCG will enhance the capability of Indian Navy and Indian Coast Guard to accurately engage small targets that post a threat to ships in an asymmetric environment, both by day and night.

This acquisition will provide further boost to the vision of “**Aatmanirbharta in Defence**“. This contract will also open up a large avenue in defence manufacturing for over 125 Indian Vendors and DPSUs for over a period of 5 years.

Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Limited (AWE) is an Indian state-owned defence company, headquartered in Kanpur, India established in 2021 as part of the restructuring and corporatisation of the Ordnance Factory Board into seven different Public Sector Undertakings.\[1\]\[2\]\[3\] AWE primarily manufactures Small arms and artillery guns for the use of the Indian Armed Forces, foreign militaries and domestic civilian use.

These remote control guns are now used by some advanced military countries like the US. Through them, army can fire guns form a remote locations while the weapon systems are fixed or positioned elsewhere. By inking the deal, the **MoD has not only saved the valuable foreign exchange and strengthened a stated owned PSU but also acquired the modern weaponry for modern warfare.**

### Background

Prior to the TAR's introduction, India largely used foreign-made [AK-style](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Kalashnikov_rifle "Kalashnikov rifle") rifles. Around 500,000 M1s were reportedly imported by India from Bulgaria in 2021 for use by the [Central Armed Police Forces](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Central_Armed_Police_Forces "Central Armed Police Forces") (CAPF) and [Indian police forces](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Indian_Police_Service "Indian Police Service").[\[4\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-BT-4) As of May 2025, India is the [second-largest arms importer](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Arms_industry#World's_largest_arms_importers "Arms industry") after [Ukraine](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ukraine "Ukraine"), accounting for 8.3% of the arms trade, according to research data from the [Stockholm International Peace Research Institute](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Stockholm_International_Peace_Research_Institute "Stockholm International Peace Research Institute").[\[5\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-5) To reduce dependence on importing small arms from other countries, part of the [Atmanirbhar Bharat](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Atmanirbhar_Bharat "Atmanirbhar Bharat") policy called for self-sufficiency to manufacture firearms in India.[\[6\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-6)

OFT announced the manufacture of an indigenous AK-based assault rifle in 2011.[\[7\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-oldnew-8) The AR was named Trichy after OFT to recognise the factory's contribution in developing and manufacturing the rifle.[\[9\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-9) Some TARs were made in 2012 to be tested.[\[10\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-Test-10) These early TARs were tested by the [Border Security Force](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Border_Security_Force "Border Security Force") (BSF), the [Central Reserve Police Force](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Central_Reserve_Police_Force "Central Reserve Police Force") (CRPF), the [Indo-Tibetan Border Police](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Indo-Tibetan_Border_Police "Indo-Tibetan Border Police") and the [Sashastra Seema Bal](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Sashastra_Seema_Bal "Sashastra Seema Bal").[\[10\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-Test-10)

Development started in 2015[\[11\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-THTAR-11) with a production line established in 2017.[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-NIETAR-12)[\[13\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-13) That March, 200 TARs were acquired by the [Chhattisgarh Police](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Chhattisgarh_Police "Chhattisgarh Police")[\[14\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-TrichyF-14) as part of the 216th Ordnance Factories Day celebration.[\[15\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-THOF-15) Concerns were raised at the time, prior to manufacture, that OFT was experiencing manpower decline, leading to a decline of employees at the company.[\[16\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-THA-16) The [All India Defence Employees Federation](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/All_India_Defence_Employees_Federation "All India Defence Employees Federation"), the [Indian National Defence Workers' Federation](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Indian_National_Defence_Workers'_Federation "Indian National Defence Workers' Federation"), and the [Bharatiya Pratiraksha Mazdoor Sangh](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Bharatiya_Pratiraksha_Mazdoor_Sangh "Bharatiya Pratiraksha Mazdoor Sangh") stated their opposition to importing small arms with the unions hoping that more orders for the TAR would be approved, retaining employees at OFT.[\[16\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-THA-16)

### Adoption

[![Image 1: Thumb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Firing_TAR_at_range.jpg/640px-Firing_TAR_at_range.jpg)](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#/media/File:Firing_TAR_at_range.jpg)

A [CISF](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Central_Industrial_Security_Force "Central Industrial Security Force") officer practices with the TAR at a shooting range.

In November 2017, the CRPF conducted field tests to determine the suitability of the TAR with 15,000 rounds fired[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-NIETAR-12) at the [CRPF Academy](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/CRPF_Academy "CRPF Academy") in Kadarpur, [Haryana](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Haryana "Haryana") with no reports of the rifle jamming.[\[17\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-17) Other tests conducted included the TAR being fired from mud, rain and saltwater and from being dropped to test reliability and accuracy.[\[18\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-CRPFTRCY-18) 100 TARs were ordered afterwards.[\[18\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-CRPFTRCY-18) In February 2018, further tests were conducted by the CRPF at Jagdalpur, Raipur, Guwahati and Srinagar with an order of 6,167 TARs placed afterwards.[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-NIETAR-12) At the time, the CRPF tested the Trichy with the Ghatak, the [Joint Venture Protective Carbine](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Joint_Venture_Protective_Carbine "Joint Venture Protective Carbine") and the [INSAS](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/INSAS_rifle "INSAS rifle")1C.[\[19\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-19) In March 2020, the CRPF acquired the first 500 out of 6,167 TARs sold to them.[\[11\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-THTAR-11)

In January 2019, the TAR was delivered to the BSF, with its Additional Director General Nasir Kamal receiving the first rifle from the [Ordnance Factory Board](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Directorate_of_Ordnance_/(Coordination_&_Services/) "Directorate of Ordnance (Coordination & Services)")'s Director General Saurabh Kumar.[\[3\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-HinduBSF-3) It was reported in the same month that the [Jharkhand Police](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Jharkhand_Police "Jharkhand Police") would acquire TARs for anti-Naxalite operations.[\[20\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-JPR-20) The TAR was displayed for the first time at the Pragati Maidan in [New Delhi](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/New_Delhi "New Delhi") for the 5th International Police Expo and the 4th India Homeland Security Expo.[\[21\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-21) In February 2020, the TAR was on public display at the Defence Expo at [Lucknow](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Lucknow "Lucknow"), [Uttar Pradesh](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Uttar_Pradesh "Uttar Pradesh").[\[22\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-DFTAR-22) It was reported at the time that the TAR was offered to the [Indian Army](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Indian_Army "Indian Army").[\[22\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-DFTAR-22) OFT reported in March 2021 that around 11,500 TARs were supplied for a total of [Rs](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Rupee_sign "Rupee sign") 1.60 billion during fiscal year 2020–21.[\[23\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-23)

In January 2021, the TriCa (Trichy Carbine) Carbine was unveiled.[\[2\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-TITR-2) Tests were conducted where 2,000 rounds were fired with no stoppages.[\[4\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-BT-4) That August, OFT announced that the TAR could use the [ARDE Under Barrel Grenade Launcher](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/ARDE_Under_Barrel_Grenade_Launcher "ARDE Under Barrel Grenade Launcher"), which was presented by OFT general manager Sanjay Dwivedi.[\[24\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-UBGL-24) A TAR variant with a downfolding stock was presented publicly.[\[25\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-PR-25) This variant was sought out by the [Railway Protection Force](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Railway_Protection_Force "Railway Protection Force") aside from the CAPFs.[\[26\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-26) In December 2021, the [National Security Guard](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/National_Security_Guard "National Security Guard") placed an order of 100 TriCa carbines.[\[27\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-NSGTriCa-27) On April 2022, the [Kerala Police](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Kerala_Police "Kerala Police") (KP) ordered 92 TriCa carbines.[\[28\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-KPTriCa-28) According to OFT, the [Greyhounds unit](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Greyhounds_/(police/) "Greyhounds (police)") ordered 44 TARs.[\[28\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-KPTriCa-28) In July 2022, the [Government of Kerala](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Government_of_Kerala "Government of Kerala") received a request from KP to procure 250 TARs with side folding stocks;[\[29\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-29) they received the TriCa carbines in May 2025.[\[30\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-KPH-30) According to the [Advanced Weapons and Equipment India](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Advanced_Weapons_and_Equipment_India "Advanced Weapons and Equipment India")'s (AWEIL) 2022–2023 Annual Report, the [National Security Guard](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/National_Security_Guard "National Security Guard") and the [Andhra Pradesh Police](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Andhra_Pradesh_Police "Andhra Pradesh Police") conducted tests on both the TAR and the TriCa carbine.[\[31\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-31)

In January 2023, the [Central Industrial Security Force](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Central_Industrial_Security_Force "Central Industrial Security Force") (CISF) received TARs manufactured from [Rifle Factory Ishapore](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Rifle_Factory_Ishapore "Rifle Factory Ishapore").[\[32\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-32) That April, Minister of State for Defence and Tourism [Ajay Bhatt](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ajay_Bhatt_/(politician/) "Ajay Bhatt (politician)") visited OFT, where he witnessed the TAR being manufactured in the factory while briefed on OFT's research and development work.[\[33\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-33) The following January, BSF procured further TARs featuring bayonets.[\[34\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-Bayonet-34) The Government of Kerala published an approved plan for the KP to acquire 30 TARs.[\[35\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-35) In November 2023, the Trichy was on display at the Dasara Exhibition in [Mysore](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Mysore "Mysore"), [Karnataka](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Karnataka "Karnataka") as part of an effort to raise awareness on crime and public safety.[\[36\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-36) In a July 2024 interview with Rajesh Choudhary, Chairman and Managing Director of AWEIL, he said that the TAR continues to be in demand with CAPFs and reported that an export order was made for the rifle.[\[37\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-AWEILI-37) In May 2025, it was reported that the Assam Forest Department and the [Central Bureau of Narcotics](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Central_Bureau_of_Narcotics "Central Bureau of Narcotics") made orders for the TriCa carbine.[\[30\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-KPH-30)

### Development

Initial versions of the TAR were produced by using [FN FAL](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/FN_FAL "FN FAL")\-based receivers and were using 7.62x39 mm magazines.[\[8\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-oldnew-8) In 2012, there were reports that the prototypes jammed during testing due to the rate of fire being 800 rounds per minutes instead of 600 rounds per minute to match with the AK-47.[\[10\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-Test-10) It was initially expected that the rate of fire would be at 650 rounds per minute.[\[10\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-Test-10)

The current version of the TAR is based on the AR-M1[\[38\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-38) with a machined receiver instead of stamped sheet to ensure the rifle has high accuracy and reliability.[\[18\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-CRPFTRCY-18) The TAR can be outfitted with [picatinny rails](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Picatinny_rail "Picatinny rail") on the upper handguard to attach scopes if requested.[\[18\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-CRPFTRCY-18)

### Combat use

In July 2021, it was reported that the TARs used by the [Kerala Police](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Kerala_Police "Kerala Police") are effective in [Naxalite-Maoist](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Naxalite%E2%80%93Maoist_insurgency "Naxalite–Maoist insurgency") [counterinsurgency operations](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Counterinsurgency "Counterinsurgency").[\[39\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-39)

On August 2025, a TAR was secured from pro-Maoist communist [Naxalite fighters](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/People's_Liberation_Guerrilla_Army_/(India/) "People's Liberation Guerrilla Army (India)") in Chhattisgarh’s [Narayanpur district](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Narayanpur_district "Narayanpur district").[\[40\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trichy_assault_rifle#cite_note-cp-40)

New Indian small arms company named "**Malhotrasons Defence Private Limited**" based in UP. The company was incorporated in 2016 according to their website.  
  
[About Malhotrasons Defence Private Limited](http://www.malhotrasonsdefence.com/about-us.html)  
  
Their 1st product for the Indian market is a 0.45 cal pistol based in the M1911 design. The pistol is named **_MSD Gauardian1911_**. They are also working on a 0.30 cal pistol based on the Russian Tokarev TT-30. These pistols are going to be offered to the military & civilian markets.  
  
You can see the 0.45 cal prototype in the video below. At the end of this video you can see the Webley WP30 0.32 cal pistol prototype. It is an original design by Webley India.  
  

  
The domestic small arms scene is getting better. Not sure if the restrictions on civilian ownership of firearms will be lowered though. Here is a video of firing test from a month or so back.  
  

  
The MSD Guardian1911 pistol looks close to being ready to be on sale. Here are a few variants on the pistol.  
  

  
Build quality seems to be pretty good.

**OFT to deliver 100 TriCa compact carbine weapon for National Security Guards**  
  
BY SPECIAL CORRESPONDENT  
TIRUCHI, DECEMBER 13, 2021 20:08 IST  
[![Image 32: 1639914318359.png](https://www.strategicfront.org/forums/data/attachments/22/22090-a599c40186c2b653829534a9bbeccb79.jpg?hash=pZnEAYbCtl)](https://www.strategicfront.org/forums/attachments/1639914318359-png.22109/)  
**It has been developed through in-house research and development**  
  
Having witnessed a significant surge in demand for its indigenously-developed Tiruchi Assault Rifle (TAR) in recent years, Ordnance Factory, Tiruchi, is poised to fulfil an order for 100 units of TriCa compact carbine weapon, also developed through in-house research and development, placed by the National Security Guards (NSG).  
  
States dealing with Naxals were keen on equipping their forces with the compact 7.72x39 mm carbine weapon, the shorter version of TAR, Officer-In-Charge of Ordnance Factory, Tiruchi, Rajiv Jain, said on Monday on the sidelines of the local public exhibition of Defence Products.  
OFT, a unit of Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Limited (AWEIL), Kanpur, is hosting the exhibition as part of the commemoration of ‘Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav’ and India@75. Tiruchi is one of the 75 locations across the country where the Ministry of Defence has instructed conduct of the exhibition of the modern defence products till December 19.  
  
OFT, has, so far, completed deliveries for 30,000 TAR weapons that are customised to meet the requirements of buyers, and will be completing the delivery of 42,000 to 45,000 units during this fiscal out of the orders for 78,000 weapons placed collectively by the Central Reserve Police Force, Border Security Force, Sashastra Seema Bal, and police forces in States, Mr. Rajiv Jain said.  
  
The exhibition started with a formal inaugural address through video-conference by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. Defence Corridor projects in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, conversion of Ordnance Factory Board into seven defence public sector undertakings were initiatives aimed at transforming India into a net exporter of defence equipment, the Minister said.  
  
Highlights among the exhibits included the Stabilised Remote Control Gun System, a lethal weapon enabling effective combat engagement while the operator remains safe below the deck, for which the OFT had developed expertise with technology transfer from Israel; and the powerful fire weapon NSV-T 12.7 mm Machine Gun AD, essentially an anti-aircraft gun developed with Russian technology, which can also be used in anti-armour and anti-personal roles, mounted on ajeyha (T-72) and T-90s tanks.  
  
The High Energy Projectile Factory, Tiruchi, a unit of Munitions India Limited, has put on display its products that included RGB-60 and its range of FSAPDS (Fin Stabilised Armour Piercing Discarding Sabot).  
  
Also on display are vintage weapons used in World War II constituting MG 15 - 7.92 mm machine gun (Germany), Fiat - Ravelli Modello 1935 Italian Medium Machine Gun, Bren .303 in MK Light Machine Gun, Berthier Light Machine Gun Mk3, Chatellerault M1924/ 29 Light Machine Gun, Vickers-Berther Light Machine Gun Mk3, Rifle No 5 MK 1, V.L. Pistol Signal 1, Luger Pistol 9mm, Welrod MK 11A 9mm Pistol, MP-40 carbine, and Sten 9mm MKS.

![Image 2: OFT to deliver 100 Trichy Carbines to NSG](https://static.toiimg.com/thumb/msid-88260803,imgsize-33362,width-400,height-225,resizemode-72/88260803.jpg)

TRICHY: Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli (OFT) has secured an order from the National Security Guard ([NSG](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/topic/nsg)) for 100 Trichy Carbines (TriCa), a mini version of (TAR).  
“While the demand for Trichy Assault Rifle (TAR) from central armed forces and state police forces is overwhelming, we have also secured an initial order to deliver 100 Trichy Carbines to the NSG,” Rajiv Jain, general manager in-charge, OFT, said on Monday.

![Image 3: 1x1 polls](https://static.toiimg.com/photo/25581306.cms)

He was speaking on the sidelines of a defence exhibition on the factory premises.  
Weighing around 3.17kg (including the magazine), TriCa is a lighter and a compact weapon compared to assault rifles.  

![Image 4: trichy_assault-rifle](https://static.toiimg.com/photo/83033472.cms)

Trichy Assault Rifle  
The factory has five new weapons at the research and development (R&D) stage.

BEL, AWEIL sign MOU

*   [January 13, 2023](https://bel-india.in/2023/01/13/)

**Bengaluru,** Navratna Defence PSU Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL) has signed an MoU with Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Limited (AWEIL), a Defence PSU, to jointly address the requirements of Indian Defence and Export markets. The MoU aims at leveraging the complementary strengths and capabilities of BEL and AWEIL to address domestic and export opportunities in the areas of Air Defence, Artillery Gun Systems, Medium Caliber Weapons, Small Arms and related systems.

Mr Dinesh Kumar Batra, then CMD, BEL, and Mr Ravin Kulshrestha, Director (Finance), AWEIL, exchanged the MoU signed between BEL and AWEIL at Defexpo 2022, in the presence of Mr Bhanu Prakash Srivastava, Director (Other Units), Mr Manoj Jain, Director (R&D), and other senior officers of BEL and AWEIL. About AWEIL

AWEIL, one of the seven DPSUs formed by the corporatisation of the erstwhile Ordnance Factory Board (OFB), is a Government of India Enterprise under the Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence. It has been incorporated as a Company under Companies Act, 2013, and is engaged in the design, development and manufacture of Defence systems such as Small Arms, Medium Caliber Weapons, Air Defence, Artillery Gun Systems, Ammunition Hardware, etc.

**About BEL**

Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL) is a Navratna DPSU under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, established in 1954 at Bengaluru, to cater to the strategic needs of the Indian Defence services. Over the years, BEL has grown into a multi- product, multi-technology, multi-unit company engaged in the design, development, manufacturing, supply and support of a wide range of Defence electronics products, systems, strategic components, services and select non-defence products, servicing the needs of customers in India and abroad.

BEL has a strong presence in Radar and Fire Control Systems, Weapon Systems, Communication, Network Centric Systems (C4I), Electronic Warfare Systems, Avionics, Anti-Submarine Warfare Systems & Sonars, Electro-Optics, Tank Electronics, Homeland Security, Gun Upgrades, Strategic Components, etc. BEL has been continuously striving to expand its solutions for the Non-Defence domain like EVMs, Renewable Energy, Energy Storage products, Smart Cities, Jammers, Software, etc. Further, BEL has diversified into Arms & Ammunitions, Seekers & Missiles, Unmanned Systems, Network & Cyber security, Medical Electronics, Space Electronics, EV, Railway/Metro and Civil Aviation to address emerging opportunities.

**Photo caption:** Mr Dinesh Kumar Batra, then CMD, BEL, and Mr Ravin Kulshrestha, Director (Finance), AWEIL, exchange the MoU signed between BEL and AWEIL at Defexpo 2022, in the presence of Mr Bhanu Prakash Srivastava, Director (Other Units), Mr Manoj Jain, Director (R&D), and other senior officers of BEL and AWEIL.

Ordnance Factory Tiruchi To Deliver 100 Trica Compact Carbine Weapon For National Security Guards
=================================================================================================

Ordnance Factory Tiruchi To Deliver 100 Trica Compact Carbine Weapon For National Security Guards

Sunday, December 19, 2021 by [Indian Defence News](https://www.blogger.com/profile/10039798451461108617)


=============================================================================================================================================================================================================

![Image 2](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEiHo_zxO87ig9F5ICupLhHGmXuNEyHWEuggd8QC3A7PZgyqpcWNPkA-d4lv0YEct9RIMIXv4xZ-hPtIrUoQVmrOJM9T3TjJtLLkEBSiVz6MTXe8zJ_ZFU3dnC8c9YkO1oH2WxMU-ReAVqVQYL1HJ7nSCoEU3cBGltPuFiD-ynVjs-l2ec04KXgG-puy4A=s16000)

  

_It has been developed through in-house research and development_

  

Having witnessed a significant surge in demand for its indigenously-developed Tiruchi Assault Rifle (TAR) in recent years, Ordnance Factory, Tiruchi, is poised to fulfil an order for 100 units of TriCa compact carbine weapon, also developed through in-house research and development, placed by the National Security Guards (NSG).

  

States dealing with Naxals were keen on equipping their forces with the compact 7.72x39 mm carbine weapon, the shorter version of TAR, Officer-In-Charge of Ordnance Factory, Tiruchi, Rajiv Jain, said on Monday on the sidelines of the local public exhibition of Defence Products.

  

OFT, a unit of Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Limited (AWEIL), Kanpur, is hosting the exhibition as part of the commemoration of ‘Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav’ and India@75. Tiruchi is one of the 75 locations across the country where the Ministry of Defence has instructed conduct of the exhibition of the modern defence products till December 19.

  

OFT, has, so far, completed deliveries for 30,000 TAR weapons that are customised to meet the requirements of buyers, and will be completing the delivery of 42,000 to 45,000 units during this fiscal out of the orders for 78,000 weapons placed collectively by the Central Reserve Police Force, Border Security Force, Sashastra Seema Bal, and police forces in States, Mr. Rajiv Jain said.

  

The exhibition started with a formal inaugural address through video-conference by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. Defence Corridor projects in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, conversion of Ordnance Factory Board into seven defence public sector undertakings were initiatives aimed at transforming India into a net exporter of defence equipment, the Minister said.

  

Highlights among the exhibits included the Stabilised Remote Control Gun System, a lethal weapon enabling effective combat engagement while the operator remains safe below the deck, for which the OFT had developed expertise with technology transfer from Israel; and the powerful fire weapon NSV-T 12.7 mm Machine Gun AD, essentially an anti-aircraft gun developed with Russian technology, which can also be used in anti-armour and anti-personal roles, mounted on Ajeya (T-72) and T-90s tanks.

  

The High Energy Projectile Factory, Tiruchi, a unit of Munitions India Limited, has put on display its products that included RGB-60 and its range of FSAPDS (Fin Stabilised Armour Piercing Discarding Sabot).

  

Also on display are vintage weapons used in World War II constituting MG 15 - 7.92 mm machine gun (Germany), Fiat - Ravelli Modello 1935 Italian Medium Machine Gun, Bren .303 in MK Light Machine Gun, Berthier Light Machine Gun Mk3, Chatellerault M1924/ 29 Light Machine Gun, Vickers-Berther Light Machine Gun Mk3, Rifle No 5 MK-1, V.L. Pistol Signal 1, Luger Pistol 9mm, Welrod MK-11A 9mm Pistol, MP-40 carbine, and Sten 9mm MKS.
